question: Which company invented the OLED, the glowing-molecule display in most flagship phones?
answer: Kodak. In 1987 Ching Tang and Steven Van Slyke, chemists at its Rochester labs, reported a thin stack of organic films that glowed when current passed through it. Kodak licensed the patents, made a few small screens, and in 2009 sold its OLED business to LG, now the leading maker of OLED television panels.
move: Invention and profit rarely happen in the same building.
source: Tang & Van Slyke, Applied Physics Letters, 1987
reference: Tang & Van Slyke, Organic electroluminescent diodes, Applied Physics Letters 51, 1987
